input.summary: Meridian's data estate spans 242 assets across 7 high-value use cases; all blocked by foundational governance gaps.
covers: Governed data foundation for AI / LLM automation
sources: Epic Clarity; Epic Caboodle; Claims administration platform; Pharmacy claims platform
Contact center transcript and telephony platform; CRM / member case management
SAS analytics estate; SQL Server reporting marts; Tableau; Power BI
Databricks on AWS (target/future-state direction — not certified current production)

story.meaning: Meridian holds a rich, multi-domain data estate — clinical, claims, pharmacy, contact center, finance — but no certified integration layer, identity spine, or governance model exists to make it decision-grade.
story.observed: 17 active assets and 225 candidates are catalogued across 7 strategic use cases. High confidence covers 174 items (72%). Every use case is blocked by at least one foundational gap: no medallion architecture, no patient/member identity spine, no formal governance operating model, and no AI audit trail.
story.matters: Without closing these foundation gaps, Meridian cannot quantify value from any use case. AI/LLM automation, cost transparency, and payment integrity all remain planning-grade hypotheses — not executable programs.
story.supports: Prioritize evidence closure in this sequence: (1) lakehouse foundation, (2) governance and semantic layer, (3) provider contract digitization, (4) transcript governance, (5) payment integrity lineage. Each gate unlocks the next tier of use cases.

findings: 242 data assets catalogued; only 17 are active — 93% remain candidate, signaling a wide execution gap between inventory and production-ready integration.

All 7 use cases share a common root blocker: no certified medallion architecture and no formal data governance operating model, making cross-use-case sequencing the highest-leverage executive decision.

Payment integrity and AI/LLM automation are the CFO's top priorities, yet SAS model lineage is ungoverned and no AI audit trail exists — both are pre-conditions for regulatory defensibility and value realization.
Provider contract terms are not digitized in governed form, directly blocking both cost transparency and provider quality use cases from advancing beyond planning stage.

breakdown.title: Data Asset Status by Use Case

rows.label: Unified Clinical + Claims Lakehouse
rows.note: EMR, claims, pharmacy — all blocked: no identity spine, no medallion arch

rows.label: Governed AI / LLM Foundation
rows.note: Prior-auth, coding, UM — blocked: no governance model, no audit trail

rows.label: Call Center Optimization
rows.note: Transcripts, CRM, claims status — blocked: no transcript governance, no intent taxonomy

rows.label: Provider Quality & Performance
rows.note: HEDIS, STAR, attribution — blocked: measure logic fragmented, attribution unproven

rows.label: Payment Integrity & Leakage
rows.note: Anomalies, FWA, billing — blocked: SAS lineage ungoverned, recovery tracking absent

chain: Data Assets & Integrations → Platform & Infrastructure (lakehouse foundation requires certified AWS/Databricks medallion architecture)
Data Assets & Integrations → Governance & Controls (all 7 use cases blocked until formal data governance operating model is established)
Data Assets & Integrations → AI & Automation (governed semantic layer and AI audit trail are pre-conditions for prior-auth, coding, and UM automation)
Data Assets & Integrations → Financial Performance (cost transparency and payment integrity use cases require claims/GL alignment and provider contract digitization)
Data Assets & Integrations → Member & Provider Experience (call center optimization and provider quality require identity linkage and attribution certification)
relationships.note: Data assets are the supply chain for every strategic use case at Meridian. Governance and platform gaps are not data problems — they are program sequencing risks that the C-suite must resolve before any use case can exit planning stage and enter funded execution.

gaps.missing: No certified medallion architecture on AWS/Databricks
gaps.blocks: Unified clinical + claims lakehouse — the foundational use case for population health, cost, and quality analytics
gaps.needed: Architecture certification with bronze/silver/gold layer evidence and Epic Clarity ingestion proof
gaps.handoff: CIO + CDAO to confirm target-state platform readiness gate before lakehouse program funding

gaps.blocks: Lakehouse, call center optimization, and any cross-domain member-level analytics
gaps.needed: Identity resolution design, source system linkage map, and loaded spine with match-rate evidence
gaps.handoff: CDAO to own identity spine as a shared platform service; assign data steward and timeline

gaps.missing: No formal data governance operating model
gaps.blocks: All 7 use cases — particularly AI/LLM automation where audit trail and data quality rule evidence are also absent
gaps.needed: Governance charter, data steward assignments, semantic layer certification, and data quality rule registry
gaps.handoff: CDAO to present governance operating model to CEO/CFO within 60 days as program gate

gaps.missing: Provider contract terms not digitized in governed form
gaps.blocks: End-to-end cost transparency and provider quality use cases — prevents margin and attribution analytics
gaps.needed: Contract digitization program with Network Contracting ownership and GL calendar alignment proof
gaps.handoff: CFO + Chief Network Officer to assign contract digitization owner and fund extraction effort

gaps.missing: SAS payment integrity model lineage ungoverned; recovery tracking absent
gaps.blocks: Payment integrity and leakage reduction — prevents CFO from quantifying or defending recovery claims
gaps.needed: Model lineage documentation, provider entity resolution proof, and investigation/recovery workflow evidence
gaps.handoff: CFO + Health Plan Ops to assign model risk owner and establish recovery realization tracking baseline

evidence.name: Data Assets & Integrations Master Catalogue
evidence.facts: 174 high-confidence items (72%); 68 medium-confidence (28%); 237 evidence references mapped across 7 use cases and 12 source systems
evidence.fields: use_case, data_domain, systems, confidence, active_candidate_status, value_hypothesis, evidence_needed, evidence_id
evidence.supports: Full use-case-to-asset mapping with system provenance and evidence gap tagging for all 7 strategic use cases
evidence.missing: No data owner assignments; no SLA or data quality metrics; no lineage or certification status per asset

evidence.name: Unified Clinical + Claims Lakehouse Evidence Bundle
evidence.rows: 3 active domain assets (EMR clinical, claims, pharmacy)
evidence.facts: All three domains sourced from Epic Clarity, Epic Caboodle, Claims administration platform, Pharmacy claims platform, and Databricks on AWS (target direction). All three share identical evidence gap: no medallion arch, no identity spine, no harmonization proof.
evidence.supports: Confirms lakehouse use case is catalogued and system-sourced but not yet integration-ready
evidence.missing: No medallion architecture certification; no identity spine load evidence; no claims/pharmacy harmonization proof

evidence.name: Governed AI / LLM Foundation Evidence Bundle
evidence.rows: 3 active/candidate domain assets (prior-auth, coding, utilization management)
evidence.facts: All three sourced from Epic Clarity, SQL Server reporting marts, SAS analytics estate, and Databricks on AWS. Governance, semantic layer, audit trail, and data quality rules are all absent.
evidence.supports: Confirms AI/LLM use case is catalogued but all four governance pre-conditions are unmet
evidence.missing: No formal governance model; no certified semantic layer; no AI audit trail; no data quality rule registry

evidence.name: Payment Integrity & Call Center Evidence Bundle
evidence.rows: 6 active domain assets across 2 use cases
evidence.facts: Payment integrity: claims anomalies, FWA, billing patterns — sourced from Claims platform, SAS, SQL Server. Call center: transcripts, CRM cases, claims status — sourced from Genesys/telephony, Salesforce CRM, Claims platform.
evidence.fields: data_domain, systems, evidence_needed, evidence_id (MER-V3-EVID-0106 to 0108; 0115 to 0117)
evidence.supports: Both use cases are catalogued with system provenance; both blocked by ungoverned lineage and missing identity/integration evidence
evidence.missing: SAS model lineage ungoverned; transcript governance absent; intent taxonomy uncertified; recovery tracking not evidenced

evidence.name: Cost Transparency & Provider Quality Evidence Bundle
evidence.rows: 6 active/candidate domain assets across 2 use cases
evidence.facts: Cost transparency: claims, capitation, provider contracts — sourced from Claims platform, Provider contract repository, GL, SQL Server. Provider quality: HEDIS, STAR, attribution — sourced from Epic Caboodle, Clarity, Tableau, Power BI.
evidence.supports: Both use cases catalogued with system provenance; blocked by contract digitization gap and fragmented measure logic across BI tools
evidence.missing: Provider contracts not digitized; GL/claims calendar alignment unproven; attribution ownership unassigned; HEDIS/STAR logic fragmented across Tableau and Power BI
